datasets.what_it_tests: a clean sales file that already carries a cost column, so margin needs no guessing
datasets.app_should: ask few or no clarifying questions, and report profit and margin as well as revenue

datasets.what_it_tests: a clean sales file with no cost column anywhere
datasets.app_should: report revenue and never invent a profit or margin figure; it may say cost data is missing

datasets.what_it_tests: duplicates, blanks that mean none, placeholder values (-1, N/A, unknown, -), outliers, a constant column, four date formats, text amounts, currency symbols and negative returns
datasets.app_should: log every cleaning action, drop the 40 exact duplicates, read the text amounts, treat -1 and the placeholder words as missing, keep the negative returns as returns, and flag the constant column

datasets.what_it_tests: a wide file: 68 columns, of which about nine matter and the rest are noise, near-duplicates or empty
datasets.app_should: find the few columns that matter (order_date, amount, category, quantity, cost_amount), say which columns are copies of each other, and not drown the report in noise

datasets.what_it_tests: a narrow file: five columns and nothing else, no ids, no cost, no customer
datasets.app_should: still produce a useful report from five columns, and not claim findings the columns cannot support (no customer, no margin, no order id)

datasets.what_it_tests: long format: one row per order line, order ids repeating, and the order-level amount repeated on every line of that order
datasets.app_should: count orders by distinct order_id and not add order_amount up once per line — the naive sum is far too high

datasets.what_it_tests: four ambiguities that each change a headline number: an unresolvable day/month order, two columns that could both be revenue, a status column mixing cancelled/returned/refunded, and zeros that could be none or missing
datasets.app_should: ask clarifying questions here rather than pick a reading silently; whichever reading it takes, the figure must match this file's reading for it

datasets.what_it_tests: three notes above the table, a merged group header row above the real header, a blank row, and a TOTAL row at the bottom
datasets.app_should: find the real header row, drop the TOTAL row from the data, and never count the total as one more bill

datasets.what_it_tests: a status column with five states and a reason column that is deliberately blank for delivered orders
datasets.app_should: treat the blank reasons as 'not applicable' rather than missing data, and report net revenue after refunds alongside gross

datasets.what_it_tests: stock levels with no money column at all: quantities, reorder levels, restock dates and damage
datasets.app_should: recognise this is stock and not sales, report what is below its reorder level and what is damaged, and never report revenue

datasets.what_it_tests: money flowing out, not in: supplier purchases with unit cost and payment status
datasets.app_should: call this spending, not revenue, and report what is still unpaid by supplier

datasets.what_it_tests: the same expense category spelled several ways (case, abbreviations, a typo, a trailing space), so the raw grouping is wrong
datasets.app_should: group the spellings together before ranking, and say it did; the raw top 3 and the tidied top 3 are different

datasets.what_it_tests: personal-looking columns (name, phone, e-mail, date of birth, emergency contact) next to real measures (pay, attendance, hours)
datasets.app_should: treat phone, e-mail, date of birth and the emergency number as identifiers, never as numbers to average or chart, and keep names out of the AI's view

datasets.what_it_tests: production batches: several material rows per batch, with the batch-level output and wastage repeated on each of those rows
datasets.app_should: count batches by distinct batch_id and not add output_units up once per material row

datasets.what_it_tests: column names in transliterated Hindi, phone numbers that must stay text, and a lifetime-spend column that is not per-order revenue
datasets.app_should: work out what each Hindi-named column means from its values, not its name, and not treat 'Kul rashi' (lifetime spend) as this period's sales

datasets.what_it_tests: a settlement statement where the money received is not the sale amount: four fee columns, GST on the fees, and negative adjustments
datasets.app_should: report net payout and sale amount as different things, and not quietly treat sale_amount as what the seller received

datasets.what_it_tests: two different subjects in one file: daily ad spend by channel, and delivery performance
datasets.app_should: keep spend, clicks, orders and delivery failures apart as separate measures, and not call ad spend revenue

datasets.what_it_tests: two files that join on customer_id, with a handful of orders pointing at customers who are not in the customer file
datasets.app_should: find the customer_id link by itself, say how many orders have no matching customer, and not silently drop them from the revenue total

datasets.what_it_tests: three files, orphan ids on both links, and one customer_id that appears twice in the customer file so a careless join inflates the row count
datasets.app_should: join on the right keys, report the orphans, and notice that the repeated customer_id makes the joined table longer than the order table

datasets.what_it_tests: five files where four form a chain (orders -> order_lines -> items, orders -> customers) and the fifth, the electricity bill, joins to nothing
datasets.app_should: link the four that connect, say plainly that the electricity bill shares no key with the rest, and not force a join

datasets.what_it_tests: the same shop's sales from two platforms: different column names, different date formats, amounts as text on one side and numbers on the other, and no shared id
datasets.app_should: see that the two files are the same kind of thing and can be stacked, match the columns across them, and give one combined total without inventing a join key

datasets.what_it_tests: margin that is only possible by joining: the sales file has no cost, the cost file has no sales, and one sold item has no cost row
datasets.app_should: join on item_code to compute margin, and say that one item's margin is unknown instead of treating its cost as zero

datasets.what_it_tests: the three sides of one shop joined on item_code: what was bought, what is in stock, and what was sold, with one item sold that neither of the other two files knows
datasets.app_should: link all three on item_code, compare bought against sold per item, and name the item code that appears only in sales
